To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of fair value based on discounted cash flow in biological assets is associated with earnings management and the quality of disclosure of the discount rates and adherence to the disclosure requirements of CPC 29 (International Accounting Standard IAS 41) is important.
the use of discounted cash flow to value biological assets is a factor in earnings management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of accounting standards in Brazil, as well as with the quality of financial reporting.

the quality of accounting and the relevance of information, as well as with the need for the IASB to consider the possibility of adopting ED/2013-08, which is currently under consultation, in the Brazilian accounting environment, since it would reduce the earnings management of companies.
the quality of accounting and the reliability of information disclosed in annual financial statements, as it is important to the decision-making process, especially for users and investors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of fair value based on discounted cash flow in Brazil is not a good practice, because it allows for earnings management, and that the use of the cost method is more appropriate, because it reduces the possibility of earnings management, as well as the disclosure requirements of CPC 29.

the use of discounted cash flow for biological assets is a source of earnings management, and that the adoption of the proposed amendment to IAS 41 would be a positive change to the accounting standard, since it would reduce earnings management.

the adoption of fair value in accounting information, in particular the discounted cash flow, is a tool that allows managers to influence accounting information, which can lead to earnings management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is no evidence that companies are manipulating earnings through the choice of a discount rate, but there is evidence that they are manipulating earnings by choosing the method of valuation, and that companies that do not disclose the discount rate have greater earnings management.

earnings management in the Brazilian market is a phenomenon that needs to be investigated further and the adoption of fair value based on discounted cash flow is not an adequate method for the valuation of biological assets.

earnings management is more evident among firms that adopt the discounted cash flow to measure biological assets, and that do not meet the disclosure requirements in the CPC 29 (2010), which is in line with the literature on earnings management in Brazil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the fair value based on discounted cash flow method is associated with greater earnings management, which is not desirable for investors.
the Brazilian accounting standard, CPC 29, does not offer a clear guidance for the measurement of fair value.

the adoption of fair value based on discounted cash flow method, which is not required in Brazil, is a tool that allows managers to manipulate earnings and the value of biological assets, which is a problem for investors and other users of financial statements.
